summary: Elkanah had two wives Hannah and Peninnah, Peninnah had children Hannah had no children, Elkanah went up yearly to Shiloh to worship sacrifice, Peninnah provoked Hannah sore to make her fret because Yahweh had shut up her womb, Hannah wept and did not eat. Elkanah says Hannah why weep, am not I better to you than ten sons? Hannah rose after eating in Shiloh, Eli sits on seat by doorpost temple, she was bitterness of soul prayed to Yahweh wept sore, vowed if you will look on affliction of your handmaid remember me not forget and give to handmaid man child then I will give him to Yahweh all days no razor shall come upon head. Eli thought she was drunk for mouth moved voice not heard, says how long be drunk put away wine, Hannah says no my lord I am woman sorrowful spirit poured out my soul before Yahweh, Eli says go in peace God of Israel grant petition, woman went ate face no more was sad, rose early worshiped returned to Ramah Elkanah knew wife, Yahweh remembered her, conceived bore son called Samuel for from Yahweh I asked him. When Elkanah went up yearly Hannah did not go for she said not until child weaned then I will bring that he may appear before Yahweh and abide forever.
whyItMatters: Hannah's barrenness to birth — mirrors Sarah, Rachel, and foreshadows Mary's Magnificat: God lifts lowly, raises poor, barren bears. Weeping to worship, bowl full to pouring out soul, vow of Nazirite child given back.

keyVerses.text: She was in bitterness of soul, and prayed to Yahweh, weeping bitterly.
keyVerses.why: Bitterness to vow — look on affliction, give back.

keyVerses.text: Hannah answered, “No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit. I have not been drinking wine or strong drink, but I poured out my soul before Yahweh.
keyVerses.why: Sorrowful spirit poured out soul — not drunk but pouring.

keyVerses.text: When the time had come, Hannah conceived, and bore a son; and she named him Samuel, saying, “Because I have asked him of Yahweh.”
keyVerses.why: Remembered — God remembers Hannah as he remembered Rachel.

questions.question: Why does Hannah weep and not eat and Elkanah says am I not better than ten sons?
questions.answer: Polygamy context — Peninnah has children provokes Hannah sore to make her fret because Yahweh shut womb. Elkanah loves Hannah double portion but says why weep am I not better than ten sons? Well-meaning but misses — husband's love doesn't erase longing for child and social shame of barrenness. Hannah's barrenness echoes Sarah, Rachel, later Elizabeth — pattern of God opening wombs of those who can't have, showing child is gift, and mother who is barren becomes mother of prophet who will anoint kings.

questions.question: What does vow 'give him to Yahweh all days no razor' mean?
questions.answer: If God gives boy, she will give him back to Yahweh all days of life, no razor on head — Nazirite vow lifelong, like Samson. Instead of keeping child for self, gives child to serve at Shiloh tabernacle under Eli. Samuel literally appears before Yahweh and abides forever — she weans (maybe 3 years) then brings to temple. Shows dedication after receiving — gift given back. Hannah's song in ch2 celebrates reversal.

questions.question: Why does Eli think Hannah drunk?
questions.answer: Eli sits on seat by doorpost of temple, sees mouth moving but voice not heard — Hannah prays silently from bitterness, lips moving, pouring soul before Yahweh. In Shiloh, drunken feasting during festival not uncommon, so Eli assumes how long be drunk put away wine. Hannah corrects not drunk but sorrowful spirit, poured soul. Eli then blesses go in peace God grant petition. Hannah's face no more sad after — after pouring, peace before answer visible. Pattern of silent prayer misread but heard by God.

glossary.def: Shafakh nefesh — pouring out inner self before Yahweh, not just reciting words.
Shemu'el — heard of God, because I asked him of Yahweh — name from asking.
Separated one with no cutting hair, lifelong dedication.
